section_summary: This section contains State Department correspondence and file records from May to November 1930 concerning the distribution of commemorative materials for the General Ulysses S. Grant monument and memorial trees in Ueno Park, Tokyo. Following the May 30, 1930 unveiling ceremony, Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville and Division of Far Eastern Affairs Acting Chief Willys R. Peck transmitted commemorative pamphlets and postcards to General Grant's descendants, Princess Cantacuzene and Lieutenant Colonel U. S. Grant 3rd. The documents include distribution letters, Princess Cantacuzene's forwarded letter to Neville, Grant's delayed expression of appreciation, an Embassy file cross-reference note, and an instruction returning Grant's acknowledgement to the American Embassy in Tokyo.

subfiles.about: Concluding page of Despatch No. 152 suggesting that commemorative enclosures regarding Ueno Park and General Grant be sent to Colonel U. S. Grant and Princess Cantacuzene.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This document is the final page of Despatch No. 152 sent by Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Edwin L. Neville from Tokyo to the Secretary of State. Neville notes a photostatic reproduction of an 1879 print showing Ueno Park during General Grant's visit and suggests that commemorative enclosures be provided to General Grant's grandson, Colonel U.S. Grant, and to Princess Cantacuzene. The despatch concludes with Neville's signature and notification of accompanying enclosures.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 152 from Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville to the Secretary of State (concluding page)

subfiles.about: Letter transmitting a pamphlet and commemorative postcards of the General Grant monument in Ueno Park to Princess Cantacuzene.
subfiles.from: Willys R. Peck, Acting Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Willys R. Peck, Acting Chief of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, transmits commemorative materials to Princess Cantacuzene in Washington, D.C., at the request of Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville. The enclosures include a pamphlet titled 'The Grant Monument and Trees in Ueno Park' and three postcards prepared for the May 30, 1930 unveiling ceremony. Two cards depict the monument and trees planted by General and Mrs. Grant, while the third reproduces an 1879 print of the park festival.
subfiles.title: Letter from Willys R. Peck to Princess Cantacuzene

subfiles.about: Letter transmitting a pamphlet and commemorative postcards of the General Grant monument and trees in Ueno Park to Colonel Ulysses S. Grant.
subfiles.from: Willys R. Peck, Acting Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Writing for the Secretary of State, Willys R. Peck sends commemorative items to Colonel Ulysses S. Grant in Washington, D.C., as requested by Chargé Edwin L. Neville in Tokyo. The items comprise a pamphlet describing the monument and trees in Ueno Park and an envelope containing three postcards produced for the dedication on Memorial Day 1930. The cards depict the memorial, the trees planted during General and Mrs. Grant's 1879 tour, and a historic print of the park.
subfiles.title: Letter from Willys R. Peck to Colonel Ulysses S. Grant
subfiles.to: Colonel Ulysses S. Grant, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference file sheet recording Despatch No. 148 enclosing Chargé Neville's Memorial Day address at the unveiling of the General Grant monument.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This State Department Document File Note indexes Despatch No. 148 dated May 31, 1930, from Chargé Edwin L. Neville in Tokyo. It records that Neville transmitted a copy of the address he delivered at the Memorial Day unveiling of the monument commemorating General Grant's visit to Japan. The sheet indexes the document under decimal classification 894.413.
subfiles.title: Document File Note for Despatch No. 148 from Japan (Neville)

subfiles.about: Handwritten letter from Princess Cantacuzene enclosing a reply for Edwin L. Neville to be forwarded by diplomatic pouch.
subfiles.summary: This partially damaged and heavily stamped document contains a handwritten incoming letter from Princess Cantacuzene sent from 1711 New Hampshire Avenue, Washington, D.C. Received in the Division of Far Eastern Affairs on June 30, 1930, it enclosed a letter addressed to Edwin L. Neville in Tokyo for transmission via diplomatic pouch. The document was recorded and officially filed on July 10, 1930, under decimal file 894.413-Grant/5.
subfiles.title: Letter from Princess Cantacuzene to the Department of State
subfiles.to: Department of State (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)

subfiles.about: Department of State letter confirming that Princess Cantacuzene's letter to Edwin L. Neville has been forwarded to Tokyo via official pouch.
subfiles.from: Willys R. Peck, Acting Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Replying to Princess Cantacuzene's letter of June 28, 1930, Willys R. Peck informs her that the Department has forwarded her enclosed letter to Chargé Edwin L. Neville in Tokyo by official diplomatic pouch. The letter is countersigned and initialed in the Division of Far Eastern Affairs and certified as a true copy of the signed original.
subfiles.title: Letter from Willys R. Peck to Princess Cantacuzene

subfiles.about: Letter of thanks from Lieutenant Colonel U. S. Grant 3rd for the pamphlet and postcards regarding the Grant Monument in Ueno Park.
subfiles.from: Lieutenant Colonel U. S. Grant 3rd, Director of Public Buildings and Public Parks
subfiles.summary: Writing on Office of Public Buildings and Public Parks stationery from the Navy Building in Washington, D.C., Lieutenant Colonel U. S. Grant 3rd acknowledges receipt of Willys R. Peck's letter of June 26, 1930. He apologizes for the delayed reply and expresses appreciation for the pamphlet and picture postcards transmitted on behalf of Chargé Edwin L. Neville. Grant notes that the materials are an interesting addition to his collection of family mementoes and requests that Peck convey his thanks to Neville.
subfiles.title: Letter from Lieutenant Colonel U. S. Grant 3rd to Willys R. Peck
subfiles.to: Willys R. Peck, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Instruction from the Secretary of State transmitting a copy of Lieutenant Colonel U. S. Grant 3rd's letter of thanks to the American Ambassador at Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the American Ambassador in Tokyo a copy of Lieutenant Colonel U. S. Grant 3rd's letter of November 13, 1930, for the Embassy files. The instruction refers back to Despatch No. 152 of June 2, 1930, from Chargé Neville. Grant's enclosed letter conveys his appreciation for the photographs and descriptive material concerning the monument unveiling at Ueno Park.
subfiles.title: Instruction from the Secretary of State to the American Ambassador at Tokyo
